topic: Sharp full-law recovery modulus at Morse-critical circular interventions. On bounded C^k causal models over T^n with grouped positive single-node perfect interventions, define complete-family Hellinger distance between observed environment laws and L2 encoder distance modulo node permutations and coordinatewise circle diffeomorphisms. Under a finite order-m derivative profile, prove the matching inverse modulus Omega_km(eps) asymptotic to eps^((k+1)/(k+m+1)), with the primary C2/Morse exponent 3/4, uniformly over both DAGs, mechanisms, and decoders. Treat CauCA plateau rotations and Varici et al. almost-everywhere exact recovery as occupied. Give a certified Fourier/spline recovery and confidence-set rung. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Multiplying every node-target baseline density and dividing by observational density^(n-1) exactly yields the decoder pushforward of an independent baseline product for any DAG. After coordinate probability-integral gauges this controls determinant error, while within-group ratios control factorization residuals, without losing the Hellinger exponent under two-sided nuisance variation. For bounded radial Hamiltonian twists, angular averaging plus interpolation through the critical hole proves the matching exponent; conditional variance of exp(i T_i) prevents quotient absorption. In the two-node C2/Morse family, exact expansions give representation error h^3 and full-law Hellinger error h^4. Ratio-only strip alternatives yield a worse exponent but incur determinant error and are excluded by the synthetic law. Checks covered anisotropic and oscillatory packets, winding, positivity, flat and coalescing critical regimes, quotient absorption, and current nonlinear/linear recovery literature; no full-modulus collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the degenerate incompressible-rigidity inequality for arbitrary bounded C2 torus diffeomorphisms in the two-node Morse model, then extend it uniformly over both nuisance classes. EARLY KILL TEST: Prove or refute the normalized divergence-free C2 inequality using joint-critical and oscillatory-strip packets; any unbounded sequence or need for extra critical-spacing/decoder assumptions pivots the run. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_circle_morse_hmod_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the complete family of positive single-node intervention laws quantitatively eliminate the volume-preserving diffeomorphism kernel after coordinate gauges at Morse-critical profiles, or can bounded C2 incompressible torus twists retain nonvanishing quotient encoder error while all environment laws converge?

source_refs.claim: CauCA constructs determinant-one, distance-dependent rotations that preserve the relevant laws while mixing coordinates on a common intervention plateau.
source_refs.author: Wendong Liang, Armin Kekić, Julius von Kügelgen, Simon Buchholz, Michel Besserve, Luigi Gresele, Bernhard Schölkopf

source_refs.claim: Density space is the quotient of the diffeomorphism group by volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, with Fisher-Rao distance given by spherical Hellinger geometry.
source_refs.author: Boris Khesin, Jonatan Lenells, Gerard Misiołek, Stephen C. Preston

source_refs.claim: Positive prescribed Jacobians with matching total mass admit regular diffeomorphic solutions, exposing freedom that determinant information alone cannot remove.
source_refs.author: Bernard Dacorogna, Jürgen Moser
source_refs.venue: Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré C, Analyse non linéaire

open_problems.why_unsolved: Determinant or density control identifies only a coset modulo incompressible maps. The first missing proof step is therefore a coercive inequality showing that within-group intervention-ratio residuals control the divergence-free remainder near the joint Morse-critical set. Classical geometric rigidity controls a matrix-well defect, whereas the available causal information consists of weighted scalar transport equations whose weights vanish at critical points. Searches combining volume-preserving rigidity, Hellinger distance, causal component analysis, and torus interventions found no result coupling these ingredients.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a normalized incompressible-rigidity inequality bounding quotient-L2 displacement of every bounded C2 torus diffeomorphism by complete-family determinant and factorization residuals with the critical exponent, or an explicit joint-critical or oscillatory sequence disproving it and identifying the minimal additional spacing or decoder restriction.

writing_exemplar.why: Its plateau-rotation obstruction provides the clearest framing for the distinction between density information and intervention-induced rigidity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Equality of pushed-forward laws constrains densities -> density constraints leave volume-preserving motions -> plateau rotations realize this ambiguity -> varying intervention factors may eliminate it except through critical holes

method_exemplars.technique: Solve the prescribed-Jacobian equation by a regular diffeomorphic construction, separating volume correction from the residual volume-preserving map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This decomposition isolates exactly the incompressible kernel that the intervention-ratio equations must subsequently control.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert an integrated local matrix-well defect into distance from one global rigid motion through a sharp geometric-rigidity inequality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is an analogous coercivity statement with weighted causal-law residuals replacing distance of a Jacobian from SO(n).

method_exemplars.technique: Express representation recovery through the error of a generic score-difference estimator and then establish concentration for an RKHS implementation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a finite-sample error interface for intervention residuals, although its linear mixer avoids the incompressible nonlinear kernel.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp inverse modulus from complete-family Hellinger distance between observational and grouped perfect-intervention laws to quotient-L2 encoder error when circular intervention-discrepancy profiles have uniformly separated Morse critical points?

source_refs.claim: CauCA proves exact identifiability under an almost-everywhere interventional-discrepancy condition and nonidentifiability through measure-preserving rotations on common plateaus.
source_refs.author: Wendong Liang, Armin Kekić, Julius von Kügelgen, Simon Buchholz, Michel Besserve, Luigi Gresele, Bernhard Schölkopf

source_refs.claim: Two hard interventions per node yield exact recovery under score-diversity conditions for general nonlinear transformations, but not a full-law quantitative inverse modulus.
source_refs.author: Burak Varıcı, Emre Acartürk, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Abhishek Kumar, Ali Tajer

source_refs.claim: Approximate nonlinear identifiability is derived under near-isometry and perturbative linear-mixing assumptions, rather than closeness of a complete family of environment laws.
source_refs.author: Simon Buchholz, Bernhard Schölkopf

open_problems.why_unsolved: CauCA and Varıcı et al. turn exact equality of laws plus almost-everywhere nonvanishing discrepancy into exact coordinatewise recovery, but neither controls the inverse when the discrepancy vanishes at isolated points. Existing approximate nonlinear-identifiability results instead impose near-isometry or perturbative linear structure. At a Morse zero, exact division by the discrepancy derivative loses uniform conditioning, while Hellinger control of pushed-forward densities retains a volume-preserving kernel. Searches for causal representation recovery combined with Hellinger moduli, Morse criticality, or a 3/4 exponent found no theorem at this boundary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching upper-and-lower quotient modulus establishing or refuting encoder error asymptotic to constant order epsilon^(3/4) for bounded C2 models with uniformly nondegenerate and separated Morse critical points, uniformly over the stated DAG, mechanism, and decoder classes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from nonlinear ICA through intervention-created identifiability to the plateau-rotation boundary is the closest motivation arc for a quantitative refinement.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nonlinear mixing makes latent coordinates nonidentifiable -> interventions create coordinate-specific derivative signatures -> a.e. discrepancy yields exact recovery but plateaus admit rotations -> isolated critical points require a quantitative recovery frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Turn approximate structural constraints into distance from a rigid transformation class using geometric-rigidity estimates and propagate the bound to latent representations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest quantitative representation-rigidity proof, although its near-isometry defect must be replaced by complete-law residuals with Morse degeneracy.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent densities as Diff(M)/Diff_mu(M) and identify the induced Fisher-Rao spherical distance with Hellinger geometry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target compares Hellinger law distance with a diffeomorphism parameter while explicitly quotienting an otherwise invisible transformation class.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate concentration error of estimated intervention score differences into probabilistic latent-recovery guarantees.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest interventional-CRL template for converting estimated environment information into representation error, but it treats linear mixers and a weaker recovery class.

open_problems.open_problem: How does the optimal law-to-encoder modulus depend on a finite order-m zero of the intervention derivative profile, and what replaces that modulus when critical points coalesce or form positive-dimensional critical sets?

source_refs.claim: The general-transformation analysis uses derivative-based score diversity for exact recovery but does not quantify conditioning near the derivative profile's zero set.
source_refs.author: Burak Varıcı, Emre Acartürk, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Abhishek Kumar, Ali Tajer

source_refs.claim: CauCA separates almost-everywhere discrepancy from positive-measure plateau failure, leaving finite-order isolated zeros between these cases quantitatively unresolved.
source_refs.author: Wendong Liang, Armin Kekić, Julius von Kügelgen, Simon Buchholz, Michel Besserve, Luigi Gresele, Bernhard Schölkopf

source_refs.claim: The quantitative Morse theorem combines quantitative Sard, inverse-function, and Morse lemmas to control critical and near-critical points of smooth maps.
source_refs.author: Tạ Lê Lợi, Phan Phiến

open_problems.why_unsolved: The first exact-recovery step that fails is division by a nonzero discrepancy derivative. It must be replaced by a bound on the measure and geometry of a near-critical tube, followed by smoothness interpolation through that tube. Isolated finite-order zeros, coalescing zeros, and critical submanifolds have different sublevel-set geometry, so an almost-everywhere condition alone cannot provide a uniform exponent. Searches for finite-type or Łojasiewicz exponents in nonlinear ICA and causal representation identifiability found no occupied target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A critical-geometry characterization giving matching upper and lower moduli for isolated order-m zeros, including whether Omega_km(epsilon) is of order epsilon^((k+1)/(k+m+1)), plus counterexample regimes or replacement exponents for coalescing zeros and positive-dimensional critical sets.

writing_exemplar.why: Its score-diversity formulation makes the qualitative derivative condition explicit and exposes the conditioning question cleanly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interventions create sparse score changes -> derivative diversity makes coordinates unique -> exact proofs ignore conditioning near null critical sets -> finite-order critical geometry should determine the recovery modulus

method_exemplars.technique: Combine quantitative Sard bounds, a quantitative inverse-function theorem, and local Morse normal forms to isolate and measure near-critical regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired characterization likewise separates a well-conditioned region from a controlled critical hole before interpolating encoder recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct prescribed-Jacobian corrections with optimal regularity and support localized to the density defect.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Localized volume corrections are natural lower-bound perturbations concentrated near finite-order critical holes.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine statistical generalization, approximation control, and numerical differentiation to propagate learned density-ratio error into latent-separation guarantees.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its derivative-error propagation is structurally analogous to estimating intervention discrepancy profiles, but it assumes globally conditioned variability rather than finite-order zeros.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a computable Fourier, spline, or needlet procedure on the torus attain the critical full-law recovery modulus and yield honest confidence sets for the encoder equivalence class uniformly over bounded nonlinear causal mechanisms and decoders?

source_refs.claim: General nonlinear transformations are handled at the population identification and achievability levels, without a finite-sample quotient recovery theorem.
source_refs.author: Burak Varıcı, Emre Acartürk, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Abhishek Kumar, Ali Tajer

source_refs.claim: The first finite-sample interventional-CRL analysis assumes a linear observation transformation and obtains recovery only up to ancestors or parent mixing under soft interventions.
source_refs.author: Emre Acartürk, Burak Varıcı, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Ali Tajer

source_refs.claim: Finite-sample nonlinear ICA is analyzed through contrastive-risk control and numerical differentiation, but not for causal intervention families, Hellinger full-law loss, or quotient confidence sets.
source_refs.author: Qi Lyu, Xiao Fu

open_problems.why_unsolved: The missing first step is not merely density estimation: simultaneous spectral bands for every environment must be converted into a complete-family Hellinger ball and then propagated through a nonlinear, nonregular inverse while minimizing over permutations and coordinate diffeomorphisms. At Morse profiles the inverse is only Hölder, so ordinary delta-method inference fails. Adaptation over unknown critical order can also conflict with honesty of nonparametric confidence sets unless self-similarity, separation, or known-order restrictions are imposed. Existing finite-sample interventional CRL remains linear, while finite-sample nonlinear ICA does not provide causal full-law confidence sets.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit truncated Fourier, spline, or needlet encoder estimator with a uniform high-probability quotient-L2 rate obtained by composing a complete-family Hellinger rate with the sharp critical inverse modulus, together with an honest confidence set having stated coverage, diameter, and necessary adaptation restrictions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction is organized around the gap between population identifiability and usable probabilistic recovery guarantees.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interventional CRL has population identifiability results -> applications provide finite environment samples -> score estimation yields rates for linear mixing -> nonlinear critical inverse maps require new rates and uncertainty quantification

method_exemplars.technique: Use localized spectral projections on a compact homogeneous manifold, prove nonasymptotic concentration for density estimators, and calibrate adaptive confidence bands.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The torus is a compact homogeneous manifold, making this a direct certified environment-density layer before propagation through the causal inverse.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate empirical contrastive-loss and approximation errors through numerical derivatives to a latent component-separation guarantee.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest finite-sample nonlinear latent-recovery proof and offers a template for controlling estimated intervention-density derivatives.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct honest L2 confidence sets over Sobolev scales using minimax tests and characterize parameter regions that must be excluded for adaptation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired uncertainty set is measured in quotient L2, and this work supplies both a construction template and the relevant honesty obstruction.

literature_map:
1. Liang et al. (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2305.17225) establish CauCA exact identifiability under a.e. intervention discrepancy and exhibit determinant-one plateau rotations when it fails.
2. Varıcı et al. (JMLR 2025, arXiv:2402.00849) obtain score-based exact recovery for general transformations using two hard interventions per node, including unknown intervention pairing.
3. Buchholz et al. (NeurIPS 2023, doi:10.52202/075280-1968) recover linear causal representations under general nonlinear mixing from unknown single-node interventions, using latent Gaussian precision geometry rather than a full-law modulus.
4. Zhang et al. (NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2307.06250) identify causal representations from soft interventions in the infinite-data regime and up to an equivalence class.
5. Hyvärinen, Sasaki, and Turner (AISTATS 2019, arXiv:1805.08651) prove auxiliary-variable nonlinear-ICA identifiability through contrastive density-ratio learning.
6. Khemakhem et al. (AISTATS 2020, arXiv:1907.04809) identify nonlinear latent-variable models using conditionally factorized exponential-family variation.
7. Lyu and Fu (ICML 2022, arXiv:2206.06593) quantify finite-sample nonlinear-ICA recovery through generalization and numerical differentiation, but not causal full-law moduli.
8. Acartürk et al. (NeurIPS 2024, doi:10.52202/079017-1243) give finite-sample interventional-CRL bounds for linear mixers and soft interventions with partial recovery.
9. Buchholz and Schölkopf (2025, arXiv:2503.15355) study approximate nonlinear identifiability under near-isometry and perturbed-linear assumptions, not Hellinger closeness of intervention laws.
10. Khesin et al. (GAFA 2013, arXiv:1105.0643) identify Hellinger/Fisher-Rao geometry with a diffeomorphism quotient by volume-preserving maps, pinpointing the incompressible kernel.
11. Dacorogna and Moser (AIHP 1990, doi:10.1016/S0294-1449(16)30307-9), Teixeira (DCDS 2017, arXiv:1608.06213), and Friesecke-James-Müller (CPAM 2002, doi:10.1002/cpa.10048) supply the nearest determinant-correction and rigidity machinery.
12. Tạ Lê Lợi and Phan Phiến (IJMA 2012, arXiv:1305.3352) quantify Morse/Sard neighborhoods, but no transfer to finite-order intervention discrepancy in causal representation recovery was found.
13. Kerkyacharian, Nickl, and Picard (PTRF 2012, arXiv:1102.2450) provide compact-manifold needlet density bands suitable for the torus observation layer.
14. Bull and Nickl (PTRF 2013, doi:10.1007/s00440-012-0446-z) characterize construction and adaptation limits for honest L2 confidence sets; no paper found propagates such sets through an encoder quotient with a critical inverse modulus.
